requested.title: Dev email outbox viewer and attachment download are unauthenticated and reachable in production deployments
/_mochi/client/stats publishes the server's module graph and absolute filesystem paths without auth
silenceInternalRoutes drops all /_mochi/* and /__mochi/admin/* log lines regardless of status or level, blinding the logs for internet-facing endpoints
/__mochi_live_reload is registered even when liveReload is false, accepting unauthenticated, untracked, unbounded WebSocket upgrades
Live-reload WebSocket upgrade performs no Origin check (cross-site WebSocket hijacking)
Public-dir reload never writes back to bunRoutes, so the next entry reload reverts the static-file table to its boot snapshot
chokidar watchers are never closed, so Mochi.stop() cannot let a dev-mode process exit
Cron handler edits silently never take effect in dev — the reload signature ignores the job's run function
Entry HMR re-applies routes, cron, image and speculation rules but silently ignores handle/csrf/protection/rateLimit/proxy changes
/__mochi/admin/page-cache admin page, JSON APIs and purge actions have no authentication layer at all

parsedVerdicts.reasoning: The code claim is exactly right: `buildEmailViewerRoutes` mounts a page that returns the whole `StoredEmail` (recipients, subject, headers, html, text) plus an API that streams raw attachment bytes, with no auth, no peer check and a self-documented 'no auth beyond that gate' comment; `clear` wipes the outbox and is reachable by any direct caller since CSRF only compares `Origin`, which an attacker sets freely. I verified the reachability chain end-to-end rather than taking it on trust: `Mochi.ts:619` gates on `development && emailTransportType === 'dev'`; `resolveEmailOptions` (email/config.ts:12) defaults the transport to `dev` whenever `development`; `packages/site/src/index.ts` passes no `email` option; the root `Dockerfile` — commented as the variant deployed for site + demos — ends in `ENTRYPOINT exec bun run dev:${WORKSPACE}` and `packages/site/package.json` defines `dev` as `NODE_ENV=development bun src/index.ts`. So `emailViewerEnabled` is true and both routes are public on the deployed hosts; nothing in site's `sequence()` or the `/demos/protection*`-scoped protection gate blocks `/_mochi/*`, and the proxy cannot blanket-block that prefix because client bundles live under it. The generic attack is concrete and does not need undelivered-mail to be harmless: with a broken/absent transport an attacker triggers a magic-link or verification mail for a victim address, reads the captured token from the public outbox, and redeems it — the token is valid to the app even though nothing was delivered. I am lowering HIGH to MEDIUM for three verified reasons: `packages/docs/170-development-mode.md:44` is an explicit 'Never run development mode in production' directive, so the mode flag is a documented boundary rather than an accidental one; the `dev` transport implies mail is not being delivered at all, narrowing the realistic exposure window; and on the two hosts actually deployed this way the impact is near-nil — `packages/site/src/demos/email/routes.ts` validates a preset id and hardcodes recipient/subject/attachment, and `packages/demos` contains no `Mochi.email()` call at all, so the outbox holds only canned demo content. The defect worth fixing is the framework's use of `NODE_ENV` as the sole authorization for a route that serves message bodies and accepts a state-mutating action.

The headline claim is empirically wrong, and I disproved it from data rather than reasoning. `ComponentRegistry.ts:1480-1483` builds each input as `toPosixPath(inputPath).replace(toPosixPath(path.resolve('.')) + '/', '')`, but Bun's metafile input keys are already cwd-relative esbuild-style paths, not absolute ones. I parsed the checked-in build output at `packages/site/.mochi/manifest.json` (whose `stats` field is literally `getClientStats()` baked at build time): of 864 unique input paths, **zero** are absolute and zero contain a `packages/` prefix — files outside the cwd appear as `../mochi/src/...`, `../docs/_components/...`, `../../node_modules/...`. There is no `/usr/src/app/...` and no `/Users/<name>/...`, so the claimed OS-account-name leak does not occur. What remains is the module graph, per-input byte sizes and the chunk import list for bundles the browser already downloads, on a site whose entire source is public on GitHub — no confidentiality boundary is crossed. The exposure on the only affected deployment is also deliberate, not accidental: the root `Dockerfile` states it runs dev mode 'so the debug bar and dev overlays are visible in the deployed environment', this page is the debug bar's own JS panel detail view, and `packages/site/src/index.ts` even ships `encodeDebugBarPaths` because the team already knows and accepts that the deployed debug bar inlines paths. Mitigations, concretely: the route is mounted only under `debugBarEnabled = development && (options.debugBar ?? true)` (Mochi.ts:503), dev mode is explicitly forbidden in production by `packages/docs/170-development-mode.md:44`, and `getClientStats()` covers client bundles plus imported CSS only — no server-only module paths reach it. The 'require explicit opt-in / restrict to loopback' recommendation still has hardening value, but there is no real security issue here as described.

The mechanism is exactly as described and I confirmed it line by line: `silenceInternalRoutes` (L431-445) branches on `path` alone, ignoring the `level` and `status` it receives in context, and `emit` applies `consoleLogger:line` at L554 — after the 5xx/slow escalation at L549 — returning early when the filter yields `null`. So a 500 or a 10-second response under `/_mochi/*` or `/__mochi/admin*` produces no output, which contradicts the filter's own docstring describing it as dropping 'framework-internal noise'. Four apps install it, including both deployed ones. The concrete, verified consequence: a 5xx from the image transform endpoint (`${assetPrefix}/image/:filename`, Mochi.ts:1707) emits a `request` event that escalates to warn and is then silently dropped, as are all request/`error`-event lines for the email viewer, client-stats page and page-cache admin. Two of the finding's most alarming illustrations are wrong, however, which is why I am downgrading it. The server-island endpoint (Mochi.ts:1559) emits **no** `request` event at all, so enumeration there is unlogged for a different reason than the filter. And 'a crashing server island is invisible to the operator' is false: Mochi.ts:1633 calls `logger.error('Server island "X" failed: …')` directly, and direct `logger.*` calls never pass through `consoleLogger:line` (only `emit()` applies it), while `island:error` has no `consoleLogger` subscription at all — so island failures do reach the log. What is left is a real but non-exploitable observability gap in an opt-in, app-chosen filter whose events remain available on `mochiEvents` for any app wiring its own pipeline; the two-line level-aware fix the finding proposes is correct, but this is a defect in the filter rather than a security vulnerability, hence BUG.

The registration defect is verified and unambiguous. `grep liveReload` across devWatcher.ts shows the file never reads `options.liveReload`, and `'/__mochi_live_reload': liveReloadHandler` is injected into the Bun route table at L635, L738 and L821 unconditionally, while Mochi.ts:1954 populates `wsHandlersMap` for that pattern only `if (liveReloadEnabled)`. With `development: true, liveReload: false` — precisely the deployed configuration, since the Dockerfile sets `MOCHI_LIVE_RELOAD=false` and site/demos map that to `liveReload: false` — the endpoint is live but unwired. For `packages/site` the upgrade genuinely succeeds (`websocket: { maxPayloadLength, idleTimeout: 30 }` is passed and chat/streams/cron declare `Mochi.ws()`, so `websocketOption` is the full dispatcher), and the orphaning claim holds exactly: `wsHandlersMap.get('/__mochi_live_reload')` is undefined, so `open`/`close` no-op and the socket never enters `liveReloadClients`. I also confirmed the reverse configuration is reachable — `packages/demos` declares only `Mochi.page`/`Mochi.api`/`Mochi.sse` (no `Mochi.ws`) and passes no `websocket` option, so on the deployed demos host `websocketOption` is undefined and the handler calls `srv.upgrade()` on a server with no WebSocket config; Bun's published docs only specify the true/false return, so whether that 400s or 500s I could not settle without running code, and I did not. I am downgrading from MEDIUM because the security framing does not survive scrutiny: `checkRouteLimit` is invoked only on the page (Mochi.ts:981) and api (1211) paths, so every user `Mochi.ws()` route is equally unmetered, and an attacker on `packages/site` can hold just as many sockets on `/demos/chat`. There is no limit or privilege actually being bypassed that the app's own ws surface does not already offer, and `idleTimeout` bounds idle sockets. What is real is the bug: the documented way to disable live reload leaves a half-wired endpoint that accepts upgrades doing nothing, and the fix (thread `liveReloadEnabled` into `DevWatcherDeps` and omit the key) is correct.

Confirmed by reading the whole file: `liveReloadHandler` (L152-172) reads `?entry`, builds `MochiWsData` and calls `srv.upgrade(req, { data })` with no reference to `Origin` anywhere in devWatcher.ts, and WebSocket handshakes are exempt from SOP and CORS preflight. This is not a speculative class — Bun's own documentation for `Bun.serve` WebSockets states it outright: 'The same-origin policy doesn't apply to WebSocket handshakes… Check the `Origin` header against an allowlist before calling `server.upgrade()`', and the framework already has `resolveExpectedOrigin`/`buildPublicUrl` in `runtime/proxy.ts` (the handler even calls `buildPublicUrl` two lines earlier). The realistic threat is the classic localhost path: a developer running `bun run dev` visits a hostile page, which opens a socket to `http://localhost:3333/__mochi_live_reload` and receives the `boot:<BOOT_ID>:<generation>` greeting (Mochi.ts:1958-1962, `liveReloadGreeting`), every `reload` broadcast, and `email:new:<id>` for each message the dev outbox captures (Mochi.ts:1979-1986). Because `notifyClients` filters on the client-supplied `__mochiEntry` against the resolved-path `affected` set, the attacker also gets a crude oracle for whether a specific absolute source path is being recompiled. Scope-limiting facts I verified and that keep this from being worse: the handler pins `__mochiRoutePattern` itself so no other ws handler is reachable, the `message` handler only answers `ping`, and on the internet-facing dev-mode deployments `liveReload: false` means `open` never runs, so the socket is never added to `liveReloadClients` and the cross-origin attacker receives nothing at all there. So the disclosure is file-save timing plus email ids on a developer's machine — low value, but a genuine missing-Origin-check on a WS upgrade with a trivial fix, and MEDIUM is the floor available for a security finding.

Traced and confirmed in full. `baseBunRoutes` is snapshotted at Mochi.ts:1827, before `registerPublicRoutes(bunRoutes, initialPublicFiles, publicRouteGuard)` runs at 1859, so by construction it never holds public routes while `bunRoutes` holds the boot-time set. `reloadPublic` (devWatcher.ts:734-744) rescans the directory, builds `nextRoutes` from `{ ...baseBunRoutes }`, calls `registerPublicRoutes(nextRoutes, …)` — which I confirmed mutates its first argument in-place (publicDir.ts:86-105) — reloads the server from `nextRoutes`, and then discards it; neither `bunRoutes` nor `baseBunRoutes` is updated. `triggerEntryReload` reloads from `{ ...bunRoutes, '/__mochi_live_reload': … }` (L631-639) whenever `counts.added.length > 0 || counts.removed.length > 0`, which restores the boot-time public set. The 404 claim also checks out: `composedFetch` (Mochi.ts:1863-1935) falls back only to registered client files, font assets and imported CSS, then `userFetch` or a 404 — there is no public-dir fallback, so a file added after boot genuinely becomes a hard 404 after an unrelated `routes.ts` edit, and a file deleted after boot is resurrected. The confusing-symptom framing is accurate because the trigger is an entry edit, not a public-dir edit, and the state heals only until the next entry reload. Note the live table is correct immediately after `reloadPublic` (it is a complete rescan from a base that includes entry-added routes via `addBunRoute`, which does write both maps) — the defect is purely the stale `bunRoutes`. Dev-only DX bug, correctly filed as BUG, and the suggested in-place rebuild is the right fix.

Verified mechanically and corroborated by the project's own notes. `startDevWatcher` creates `chokidar.watch(finalWatchPaths, …)` at L693 and `chokidar.watch(svelteConfigPath, …)` at L810 and returns only `watcherReady` (L826) — no dispose handle — and `grep '\.close()\|unwatch'` across all of `packages/mochi/src` returns nothing, so neither watcher is ever closed anywhere in the framework. The teardown wrapper on `server.stop` (Mochi.ts:2032-2067) stops the image sweeper, memory-pressure handler, cron runtime, email-badge subscription, email transport and every rate-limit store, but it is installed at 2032 while `startDevWatcher` is not called until 2152, and `runShutdown` (2236-2275) adds nothing. The signal path escapes only by force-exiting, and its comment names the exact cause ('chokidar's dev watchers … would otherwise keep the event loop alive past the last socket', Mochi.ts:2213); `utils/shutdownSignalServer.ts:15` independently confirms it from the project's own test harness ('Dev mode is the case that hangs in practice: it starts chokidar watchers that outlive the last socket'). `Mochi.stop()` → `performShutdown()` → `runShutdown()` never calls `process.exit`, and its JSDoc at 2188-2191 explicitly promises to stop 'without exiting the process, so a finite-lifetime embedder (script, test) can end naturally' — a promise the dev path cannot keep. The secondary claim is also sound: the surviving watchers keep invoking `recompileChanged`/`server.reload`/`notifyClients` against a stopped server, pinning the registry and compiled module graph. Not a security issue; correctly filed as BUG, and returning a disposer wired into the stop wrapper is the right fix.

Confirmed on both halves of the chain. `cronSignature` (cron.ts:78-79) hashes `JSON.stringify(jobs.map(j => [j.name, j.schedule, j.options?.tz ?? null, j.options?.dev ?? true]).sort())` — the `run` function is deliberately excluded — and `reconcileCron` (devWatcher.ts:369-388) returns early whenever that signature is unchanged. I then verified that re-registration is the only way a new handler can take effect: `startCronRuntime` (queue.ts:933+) is the sole path that registers handlers, and it does so via `await boss.work(queueName, cronWorkOptions, cronWorkHandler(job))`, where the handler closes over the `job` object and therefore over that build's `job.run`. Since `buildEntry` re-imports the entry fresh (`extractServeOptions(outFile, { fresh: true })`) but the new job objects never reach `startCronRuntime` when the signature matches, the scheduler keeps executing the closure captured at boot — against the *old* module instance's state — for the rest of the session. The contrast the finding draws is real: `reloadImage` immediately below does warn for its boot-only fields (L390-400), route handlers are genuinely hot-swapped in `applyRouteChanges`, and `packages/docs/118-scheduled-jobs.md:114` tells users 'In development, editing the `cron` array re-registers on save — no dev-server restart needed', which a developer will read as covering handler edits even though strictly it says 'array'. Silent staleness with no warning is an expensive debugging trap and actively dangerous when the job writes a database or sends mail. Correctly filed as BUG; the cheapest honest fix is the one-time warning plus a docs clarification.

Verified by enumerating every consumer. `buildEntry` (devWatcher.ts:342-360) re-extracts the full `MochiServeOptions` and reapplies exactly four fields — `speculationRules` (347), `cron` (348), `image` (349) and `routes` (350-360) — discarding the rest. On the server side `const middleware = options.handle` is captured once at Mochi.ts:505 and is the only reference used by the page closure (991), the api closure (1240) and `composedFetch` (1922); `makeRequestContextBuilder` is likewise constructed once (772-784) with `proxy`, `csrf`, `trailingSlashPolicy`, `cookieDefaults`, `development`, `debugBarEnabled` and the protection gate frozen in, and `composedFetch` reads `options.csrf`/`options.proxy` off the boot options object (1865). A re-imported entry produces a brand-new options literal, so none of those can change — contrast `shellTemplate` and `speculationRules`, which are deliberately read through mutable getters/setters. The silence is also real: with only `handle` edited, `counts` stays all-zero so no 'Entry rebuilt' line prints, yet the file change still emits `recompile:complete`, so `consoleLogger` prints an 'HMR src/index.ts … rebuilt 0 pages' line that reads as a successful reload. The security-adjacent failure mode the finding highlights is the right one to call out — `packages/support` gates every `/admin*` path through `sequence(adminAuth)` in `handle`, so a developer iterating on that chain is testing the pre-edit version while being told the reload succeeded. Not itself exploitable, so BUG is the correct severity; mirroring the `reloadImage` warning for the boot-only key set is the proportionate fix.

I read the file in full and there is nothing to exploit. `serverProps` returns the module-level constants `STUB_STATS` (`{ size: 3, totalBytes: 12345 }`) and `STUB_ENTRIES` (three hardcoded fake rows for `/`, `/docs/intro`, `/api/health`), and the two JSON endpoints return those same constants — none of it is derived from any runtime cache, request or filesystem state. The actions are inert by construction: `purgeAll: () => undefined` and `purge: ({ formData }) => { formData.get('path'); return undefined; }`, i.e. the value is read and dropped, so no state is mutated and there is nothing to flush. So neither of the two impacts the finding describes — cache-key enumeration and an unauthenticated cache-flush DoS — exists today; the finding itself concedes 'the current data exposure is nil' and reports on the basis of an implementation that has not landed. The mount gate is `debugBarEnabled` (Mochi.ts:790), the same dev-mode flag covered under F2, and dev mode in production is explicitly forbidden by `packages/docs/170-development-mode.md:44`; being in a different file this is not a duplicate of F2 under the stated rules, but it inherits that premise without adding any present-day impact. The two side observations are accurate and worth keeping as design notes — `PAGE_CACHE_ADMIN_PATH` is a hardcoded `/__mochi/admin/page-cache` literal rather than derived from `assetPrefix`, so it does not move with a relocated prefix, and the purge actions will need a real credential rather than a mode flag when the page cache ships — but a security review cannot call a route serving three fake constants and discarding its inputs a vulnerability. Anticipatory, not real.
